stem: An online store shipped 500 orders last week. Of these orders, 320 were sent by standard delivery and the rest were sent by express delivery. Of the express orders, 90% arrived on time, and a total of 46 orders arrived late. If one of the orders that arrived late is selected at random, what is the probability that it was sent by express delivery?
solution: Of the 46 late orders, 18 were express.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This divides the 18 late express orders by all 500 orders instead of by the 46 late orders.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the probability that a late order was sent by standard delivery, \(\frac{28}{46}\).
explanation.C: Correct. 18 of the 46 late orders were express, and \(\frac{18}{46} = \frac{9}{23}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the probability that an express order arrived late, \(\frac{18}{180}\); the condition is reversed.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'B': 'A', 'D': 'B', 'C': 'C', 'A': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'B', 'B': 'D', 'C': 'C', 'D': 'A'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
ex = 500 - 320
late_ex = ex - Rational(90, 100) * ex
assert late_ex == 18
p = late_ex / 46
assert p == Rational(9, 23)
assert value(choices[answer]) == p
assert all(value(choices[k]) != p for k in choices if k != answer)
